alignments.note: Waw of the consecutive form takes the *And* (rule 14).
Finite verb with its English subject pronoun (rule 17).
Substantival article takes the supplied pronoun plus relative *that which* and heads on *that* (rule 41).
The substantivized adjective keeps its own English together with the supplied copula, which stays with the predicate word (rules 20, 41).
Preposition.
Construct noun; no article morpheme stands in the chain, so the supplied *the* joins it (rule 29).
Nomen rectum with the relational *of* (rule 19).

`כְּ` rendered by the compound preposition *according to*, one rendering of which no part belongs to another morpheme (rule 30); headed on *according*, the word carrying the relation rather than the connective (rule 24).
Relative particle.
Finite verb with its auxiliary, headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Proper name; the ASV reorders the appositional name after *father*.
Noun.
Pronominal suffix rendered by the possessive *his* (rule 18).
The restrictive particle `רַק` is what the ASV's adversative *howbeit* renders; no waw stands at the head of this clause, so the connective is not rule 14's.
Negative; the ASV postposes it after the verb, so the neighbouring units are discontinuous around it (rule 25).
Finite verb with its subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb.
Preposition.
Construct noun with no article morpheme in the chain, so the supplied *the* joins it (rule 29).
Nomen rectum with the relational *of* (rule 19).
Conjunction.
`עוֹד` → *yet*; English places it inside the verb phrase, so the participle's unit is discontinuous around it (rule 25).
Article → *the* (rule 15).
Noun.

Hiphil participle rendered by the light verb plus adverbial complement *did ... corruptly*, headed on the complement that carries the lexeme (rule 44); discontinuous around *yet* (rule 25). Heading on *did* was available but would give the verb's English auxiliary the lexeme.

review_notes: `רַק` takes *howbeit* here; the word is in rule 14's connective list, but no waw opens this clause, so the restrictive particle is the morpheme that licenses it.
*did ... corruptly* is read as one light-verb rendering of the participle rather than as a supplied verb plus adverb, since dropping *corruptly* loses the lexeme (rules 31, 44).
